description: We are a multidisciplinary team in the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge, combining Hydrology, Geomatics, Environmental Sciences, and Software Engineering. We aim to use NASA Earth observation data, soil information, and crop characteristics to develop a practical decision-support tool that helps farmers in Pakistan adapt to climate change, water scarcity, and extreme weather.
summary:
SoilPulse: NASA Data for Smarter Farming

SoilPulse is a decision-support application helping farmers in Punjab make climate-smart crop rotation decisions using NASA Earth observation data and local agricultural information.

Our Sheikhupura demonstration identified **4,678 fields**, including **237 bare fields covering 189.2 hectares**, using satellite imagery.

By combining climate, soil, rainfall, evapotranspiration, and water data, SoilPulse compares crop rotation strategies for water conservation, soil protection, and sustainable agriculture.

With GPS field detection, multilingual support, and voice interaction, it turns complex satellite data into practical recommendations while keeping farmers in control.
details:
What It Does & How It Works:

SoilPulse (built for "Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data") is a farmer-centered decision-support web application that transforms NASA Earth observations and local soil data into clear, money-saving crop rotation plans[cite: 1]. Most smallholder tools fail because farmers lack digital government land boundary files[cite: 1]. SoilPulse solves this automatically: a user simply draws a box on the map or taps GPS, and our satellite pipeline removes roads, canals, and villages to outline individual farm parcels on its own[cite: 1]. In our Sheikhupura, Pakistan testbed, SoilPulse automatically delineated 4,678 individual farms and flagged 237 uncovered (bare) parcels covering 189.2 hectares—pinpointing the critical May–June post-wheat fallow window[cite: 1].

For any selected farm, SoilPulse blends 10 years of NASA POWER weather and heatwave history, NASA SMAP root-zone soil moisture, GPM rainfall, GRACE-FO groundwater trends, and SRTM 3D terrain slope with ISRIC SoilGrids (global) and USDA SSURGO/CropScape (U.S.) soil and crop history[cite: 1]. It then compares four practical rotation strategies side by side—Current Practice, Natural Fertilizer (Legumes), Water & Pumping Saver, and Soil & Erosion Protector—showing the satellite evidence, expected savings, data gaps, and local risks for each[cite: 1].

Benefits & Intended Impact:

- Water & Pumping Savings: Identifies moisture deficits and recommends shifting from water-heavy monocultures to DSR rice, maize, sorghum, or winter pulses—reducing diesel and electric pumping costs by 20–45%[cite: 1].

- Lower Fertilizer Bills: Recommends nitrogen-fixing legumes calibrated by growing window—fixing 40–60 kg N/ha with a 60-day summer catch crop (Mungbean or Sesbania/Jantar) in the May–June bare gap[cite: 1], or 100–140 kg N/ha with full-season legumes (Berseem clover or Soybean).

- Topsoil Protection: Shields bare summer soil from extreme heatwaves and July monsoon washout[cite: 1].

- Inclusive Last-Mile Reach: Empowers low-literacy and non-literate smallholders to make climate-resilient decisions without needing technical or English literacy[cite: 1].

Creativity & Key Differentiators:

1. Cooperative Village Cluster Mode: Farming does not happen in isolation. Clicking any bare farm (such as Field #1371, 1.52 ha) scans a 500-meter radius for neighboring bare plots—identifying 16 adjacent empty farms forming a 15.7-hectare community block[cite: 1]. Synchronizing cover crops across neighbors blocks cross-border pest migration, saves ~31 bags of synthetic urea, and cuts shared tractor/harvester costs by 25%[cite: 1].

2. Zero-Literacy Voice & Traffic-Light Interface: Our dedicated "Farmer Helper" mobile view replaces technical charts with simple Red/Yellow/Green traffic-light health cards and 1-tap GPS farm detection across five languages (Urdu, Punjabi, Sindhi, Pashto, and Simple English), allowing farmers to listen to spoken summaries and ask questions by voice[cite: 1].

Tools, Languages & Software Used:

- Backend & Geospatial Engine: Python (FastAPI, Uvicorn, Pandas, GeoPandas, Shapely, Google Earth Engine API, gTTS for spoken Urdu/English audio, pure-Python EPSG:5070 coordinate transformation).

- Frontend: Lightweight, zero-build HTML5, CSS3, Vanilla ES6 JavaScript, Leaflet.js (Canvas renderer for 4,678 polygons), custom inline SVG climate charts, and browser MediaRecorder voice capture.

- AI & Data APIs: Google Gemini 2.5 Flash (multimodal voice and text advisory), NASA POWER, NASA SMAP, GPM IMERG, ECOSTRESS, GRACE-FO, SRTM DEM, NASA GIBS WMS, NASA AppEEARS, ESA Sentinel-2 & WorldCereal, ISRIC SoilGrids v2.0, USDA-NRCS SSURGO, USDA CropScape CDL, and OpenStreetMap Nominatim.

- Deployment: Hosted live on Vercel (frontend) and Render (backend) for fast loading on low-bandwidth rural mobile networks.

Factors Considered (Human-in-the-Loop Ethics):

Our team prioritized satellite-to-field scale transparency, rural mobile bandwidth constraints, and farmer autonomy. Because satellites can measure heat, rain, and greenness—but cannot see subsurface soil salinity, delayed canal water turns, or local market prices—every recommendation includes a confidence indicator and a "1-Tap Reality Check" ("Canal Water Delayed", "White Salt Crust", "No Machinery") that updates crop advice instantly while reminding farmers to verify final choices with local agriculture officers
